h1: The S.G. Hotel Buriram — a budget city-centre hotel with a pool near Chang Arena
intro: If you're coming to Buriram on a tight budget but still want a clean room with a pool to cool off in, somewhere central where you can walk out for food, and close enough to drive to a match at Chang Arena or a race at Chang International Circuit without much fuss — The S.G. Hotel Buriram is a name that comes up often in reviews of budget hotels. It's a small 3-star place with about 30 rooms on Jira Road, Isan sub-district, within Buriram's municipal area · rooms start at around THB 750/night, and real guest reviews across several platforms agree on the cleanliness, the value and the in-town location.

body.html: The S.G. Hotel Buriram overview — who it suits — To put it the way you'd tell a friend, this is a small budget hotel that nails the "good value, clean, in town" combination at a price most people can pay comfortably · The building is a 3-star property with about 30 rooms on Jira Road, Isan sub-district, within Buriram's municipal area, a central part of town where you can walk out to restaurants, cafés and markets · What makes it more interesting than many places at the same budget is that it has an outdoor pool to swim in, free parking, and some rooms have balconies overlooking the pool — things you don't often get in hotels priced in the high hundreds to low thousands of baht · It's been open since around 2015 · From the real guest reviews gathered across several booking sites, the people it suits best are budget travellers who want a clean room in town, couples on a short trip, backpackers and solo travellers focused on value, and small families who want a pool for the kids without paying a lot · Another good fit is football fans and motorsport followers coming for a match at Chang Arena (i-mobile Stadium) or a race at Chang International Circuit who want to stay in town for the wider choice of places to eat and then drive out to the venue · This isn't a luxury resort or a design-heavy boutique hotel, but it's a straightforward place where you get what you pay for and then some — and most people leave feeling they got more than the price.

Location and getting around — The hotel's actual address is 555/1 Moo 8, Jira Road, Isan sub-district, Mueang Buriram district, within the municipal area — a central location that's convenient if you mainly want to base yourself in town · Around the hotel there are restaurants, cafés, convenience stores and markets within easy walking distance for finding something to eat — some reviews mention walking to the night market or walking street (Lively Market / Saraka Market) and several restaurants nearby · Thawikit Supercenter is close, about 350 metres away, handy for stocking up · For those coming for the sport, this location is about a 10–15 min drive to Chang Arena (i-mobile Stadium) and Chang International Circuit, roughly 6 kilometres away · You can take a Grab or a motorbike taxi to the venue cheaply, or if you drive yourself it's easy since there's free parking · Other transport reference points: Buriram railway station is about 3–4 kilometres away, while Buriram Airport (BFV) is fairly far at about 35 kilometres, or roughly a 40 min drive, which is normal for Buriram since the airport is outside town · One thing worth knowing: some international reviews say "the hotel entrance is a little hard to find from the main road," so on your first visit open a map and watch for the signs, and on days with a big match or major race, the roads in town get especially busy — allow extra time to reach the venue.
"Clean room, helpful staff, in town and easy to walk out for food, very cheap for what you get, and there's a pool to swim in too. Great value for a short stay in Buriram."

Room types and décor — The S.G. Hotel is a small hotel with about 30 rooms, decorated simply and cleanly in budget-hotel style — nothing flashy, but everything you need · The room types you'll most often see on booking sites are Superior Double Room (one large bed) and Superior Twin Room (two single beds), and at certain times there are Deluxe rooms that are larger or look out over the pool · Every room has air conditioning, a fridge, a flat-screen (LED) TV, a private bathroom with a shower, a kettle and free Wi-Fi · A point many reviews mention positively is that some rooms have a private balcony overlooking the pool — a nicer spot for morning coffee than the price would suggest · Real guest reviews agree that the rooms are clean, the beds comfortable, and the TV and Wi-Fi work fine, with the room space being just right for a short stay · To be straightforward, there are also a few notes from reviews worth knowing: some say the beds are fairly firm for anyone who likes a soft mattress, the internet in some rooms isn't always stable, English-language TV channels are limited, and the hot water in some bathrooms may not be strong or consistent · These are normal for a budget hotel, not unexpected flaws, but if you're a light sleeper or specifically need a soft mattress, set your expectations to the price level or ask the hotel about the bedding before you stay.

Facilities and the pool — The selling point that sets The S.G. Hotel apart from many same-budget hotels in Buriram is the outdoor swimming pool · For a hotel in the high-hundreds to low-thousands baht range, having a pool to swim in is a bonus that many reviews rank among the top positives, especially for families with kids or anyone who wants to cool off after a full day out · Besides the pool there's free private parking on site, which suits people driving themselves or renting a car to tour the Buriram–Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam route · There's an in-house Thai restaurant, a small bar/lounge for a drink, a garden, front-desk luggage storage, and at certain times a bicycle-rental service for getting around town · Free Wi-Fi covers the common areas · Overall the facilities aren't extensive like a big hotel's, but they're enough for a stay in town, and having both a pool and free parking at this price is what pushes the value rating high in guests' eyes · Worth knowing: the pool is a modest size meant for soaking and cooling off rather than a long pool for serious lap swimming, and you should check the pool's opening hours with the hotel on the day of your stay.

Food and bar — The hotel has an in-house Thai restaurant and a small bar/lounge for an evening drink · On breakfast we have to be honest: the information differs across booking platforms — some list a simple breakfast (toast, tea, coffee, fruit, cereal, light Thai-style options), while others say breakfast isn't included in the room rate · So if breakfast matters to you, check the terms on the booking page clearly before you book to see whether the package you choose includes it · The upside of the central location is that this isn't a big problem, because around the hotel there are breakfast spots, cafés, congee/rice-soup shops and markets within easy walking distance, so many people choose to eat out for the variety and the lower prices · Some international reviews praise the hotel's Thai restaurant for tasting good at friendly prices, handy for a simple meal when you don't want to go out · Overall, food here isn't a reason to come and eat in the hotel as your main plan, but it's a decent add-on, and the in-town location fills the gap well.

Service — Service is an area that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews · Several staff are mentioned as being friendly, cheerful and helpful, from check-in through to recommending restaurants and places to visit around town · There's a reception desk for questions and luggage storage · For travellers coming for a race or a match at Chang Arena, staff can help call a car or suggest the route to the venue · To be straightforward, since it's a small hotel the staff numbers aren't as large as a big hotel's, so when the hotel is full or there's a big event in town, response times may be a little slower, and there's one older review that once had an issue over being charged for a damaged towel (which the guest disputed) — a one-off case that doesn't reflect the overall picture, but noted for completeness · Overall the service is good and better than expected for a hotel at this price, and it's one reason the review scores on several platforms sit high.

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — Gathered from Trip.com, Agoda, Hotels.com, Expedia and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent within the budget-hotel category · On the praise side: clean, well-kept rooms; beds comfortable for a short stay; a pool to swim in at a budget price; free parking; friendly, helpful staff; a central location within walking distance of restaurants and markets; and the most-mentioned point of all, value for money — many say they got more than they paid for, and some couples rate the location as high as the low 9s · On some platforms the overall score sits in the 8–9 out of 10 range, which is good for a 3-star hotel at this price · On the notes side: the beds in some rooms are fairly firm; the Wi-Fi/internet in some rooms isn't always stable; English-language TV channels are limited; the hot water in some rooms isn't strong; the hotel entrance is hard to find from the main road on the first try; and the breakfast terms are unclear across platforms · Most of these are things you can manage by setting expectations to the price level and checking the details before booking, rather than big problems that keep people from coming back.

"Great value for coming to watch football in Buriram. Clean room, a pool, free parking · The only downside was the bed being a touch firm for us, and finding the entrance was a bit tricky the first time, but for this price it's really very okay."

Price comparison and value — The starting price for a Superior room is around THB 750/night at normal rates (some promotional periods drop into the high hundreds, around THB 700) and can climb to roughly THB 900–1,200 over long weekends or on days with a big match/race at Chang · Compared with hotels in central Buriram at a similar price, The S.G. Hotel feels good value among budget hotels with a pool, because most places at this budget don't have both a pool and free parking · If you step up a level to a 4-star boutique hotel like The Crystal Hotel (formerly X2 Vibe), starting around THB 1,400/night, or stadium-zone hotels like Modena by Fraser and Amari Buriram United at higher prices, you'll get better rooms and facilities to match · But for anyone focused on saving money who just wants a clean bed in town, plus a pool as a bonus, The S.G. Hotel fits this budget well · The tip is to compare prices across several platforms — Agoda, Booking and Trip.com — before booking, because for a small hotel like this the prices and terms (such as whether breakfast is included) vary by period and by site.

Good to know before you book — A few small things help your stay go more smoothly · One, check the breakfast terms on the booking page clearly to see whether it's included, since the information differs by platform; if it's not included, don't worry, as there are plenty of places to walk to around the hotel · Two, if you like a soft mattress or are a light sleeper, ask the hotel about the bedding first, or be prepared that a budget-hotel bed may be fairly firm · Three, on your first visit use map navigation and watch for the signs, because reviews say the hotel entrance is hard to find from the main road · Four, if you come during a big Buriram United match at Chang Arena or a major race at Chang International Circuit, rooms fill up fast and prices rise — book several days ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate · Five, if a pool view matters, ask for a room with a balcony overlooking the pool when you book · Six, if you drive yourself, just use the free parking at the hotel, handy for touring the Phanom Rung–Mueang Tam route.

The bottom line — From all the real reviews, The S.G. Hotel Buriram is a hotel that delivers high value among Buriram's budget accommodation — clean rooms, a pool to swim in, free parking, friendly staff, and a central location within walking distance of restaurants and markets · What makes it especially interesting is having a pool in a hotel priced in the high hundreds to low thousands of baht, which isn't common · If you're looking for a luxury hotel, design-heavy rooms, a premium soft mattress, or you really want to stay right by the stadium gates on race day, this may not be your first choice, and you should consider a boutique or stadium-zone hotel at a higher price · But for budget travellers, couples on a short trip, families who want a pool for the kids, or football fans and motorsport followers who want to stay in town and drive to Chang in just over ten minutes — The S.G. Hotel Buriram is the option that costs little but covers the essentials, and it's the reason the review scores on several platforms stay consistently good.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — The S.G. Hotel Buriram

faq.q: Where is The S.G. Hotel Buriram · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 555/1 Moo 8, Jira Road, Isan sub-district, Mueang Buriram district, within the municipal area · within walking distance of restaurants, markets and Thawikit Supercenter (about 350 m) · about a 10–15 min drive to Chang Arena (i-mobile Stadium) and Chang International Circuit, roughly 6 km away · Buriram railway station is about 3–4 km away, and Buriram Airport about 35 km.

faq.q: Does The S.G. Hotel Buriram have a pool?
faq.a: Yes · the hotel has an outdoor swimming pool to cool off in, which is a highlight because it's not common in budget hotels at this level · some rooms also have a balcony overlooking the pool · check the pool's opening hours with the hotel on the day of your stay.

faq.q: What's the starting price at The S.G. Hotel Buriram · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 750/night for a Superior room (some promotional periods drop to around THB 700) · there are Superior Double (large bed), Superior Twin (two single beds) and Deluxe/pool-view rooms depending on the period · prices rise over long weekends and on days with a big event at Chang — compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is it good for coming to watch football or a race at Chang?
faq.a: Yes · the location is central, about a 10–15 min drive to Chang Arena (i-mobile Stadium) and Chang International Circuit · the upside is that staying in town gives you plenty of places to eat and free parking · the note is that you won't be right by the stadium gates, and on big race days rooms fill fast and the roads get busy — book ahead and allow extra time.

faq.q: Does The S.G. Hotel Buriram have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: There's free private parking at the hotel, plus an in-house Thai restaurant and a bar/lounge · for breakfast, check the terms on the booking page clearly because the information differs by platform — some packages include it, some don't · if it's not included, you can easily walk out to a place in town.

faq.q: What are the things to note or watch out for at The S.G. Hotel Buriram?
faq.a: From real reviews: the beds in some rooms are fairly firm for those who like a soft mattress, the Wi-Fi in some rooms isn't always stable, the English TV channels and the hot water in some rooms have limits, and the hotel entrance is hard to find from the main road on the first try — use map navigation · these are normal notes for a budget hotel; set your expectations to the price level and you'll stay comfortably.
